problem: Kemble's trip to the mill was in the last week of March or first week of April 1848 (Encyclopedia.com, 'Kemble, Edward'); BYU RSC dates the Star's 'sham … takein' item to 20 May 1848 and does not attribute it to Kemble by name. 'May (before mid-month)' fits neither.

fix.digest: Edward Kemble, who ran the Star for Brannan, went up to Coloma with a party in late March or early April and came back unconvinced; Reading's panning there had produced almost nothing. The Star then dismissed the gold reports, and an item dated 20 May called them a sham and a take-in got up to fool the gullible. Events overtook the paper within weeks.
fix.source_note: Encyclopedia.com, 'Kemble, Edward' (visit, late March/early April 1848); BYU RSC 'Saints and Gold: 1848' (Star item, 20 May 1848).

problem: Levy cites The Star of 21 December 1895 only as 'Cf.' for the roughly 18-month delay in promulgating the pass regulations the Chamber drafted in 1894. He does not say what The Star reported that day. The digest says more than the source.

fix.digest: Norman Levy cites The Star of 21 December 1895 on the pass regulations for African mineworkers that the Chamber had drafted in 1894 and that the government promulgated only after a delay of about eighteen months. The regulations, backed by the Master and Servant law, were meant to tighten the owners' control over the movement of African workers. Eight days later Jameson's force crossed the border.
fix.source_note: Levy, 'The state, mineowners and labour regulation', note 20 (cites The Star, 21.12.1895, as 'Cf.'); SAHO timeline (29 December 1895). The Star's own report was not consulted.
